Alex (infra): kicking off my handoff — primary here for the evening. quick snapshot: we had a p95/ p99 blip in eu-west around 19:22 UTC that resolved after autoscale burst, but a small set (~3 customers) saw elevated 502s. leaving notes + runbook pointers.

IncidentBot: PAGER TRIGGERED — INCIDENT-2234 — inference.latency.p99 eu-west increased > 2s for 7m :rotating_light:

Jamie (sre): saw that, good catch. is the KV cache thrashing metric high?

Alex (infra): KV cache eviction rate spiked then normalized. suspect prefix-cache miss storm from a big batch job. linked the query trace here: https://internal.redwood/run/trace/2234.

Priya (platform): customer-impact summary? support asked for an ETA.

Mia (support): affected customers: acme-co, betacorp, and internal QA. acme-co reported ~30 failed requests at 19:22 — most retries succeeded. ticket #SUP-4921.

Marcus: were model fallbacks engaged?

Alex (infra): yes, smart-routing briefly routed to low-cost variant (model:small-v1) for best-effort capacity. no data loss. latency/p50 normal, but p99 affected.

Jamie (sre): quick mitigation checklist I'm leaving in the thread (fastest first):
1) Toggle routing to avoid small-variant fallback: run on-call CLI -> ``rwdctl route update --region eu-west --policy prefer=primary``
2) Throttle the noisy prefix: ``rwdctl kvcache throttle --prefix <prefix> --rate 50/s``
3) Trigger a controlled batcher warmup: ``rwdctl batcher warmup --model primary-model --region eu-west --workers 4``
4) If errors persist > 10m, scale dedicated pool: ``rwdctl capacity scale --pool inference-eu --replicas +2``

Priya (platform): adding links to runbooks: lightweight recovery runbook (KV-cache/eviction): https://docs.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction-guide
Model fallback & routing playbook: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/routing-fallbacks
Paging/escalation matrix: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/paging-and-escalation

Alex (infra): practical commands I ran earlier (paste):
```
# force immediate route to primary models
rwdctl route update --region eu-west --policy prefer=primary
# pause prefix-heavy traffic (used for noisy batch job)
rwdctl jobs pause --job-id job-9876
# bump pool quickly
rwdctl capacity scale --pool inference-eu --replicas +1
```

Mia (support): I already informed acme-co and betacorp with note: "We observed transient increased latency 19:22–19:29 UTC, little/no customer-visible data loss; retries succeeded for most requests. engineering investigating." They asked for postmortem email.

Marcus: ok. any known config that caused prefix miss storm?

Alex (infra): preliminary root cause theory: a scheduled internal scoring job started with a new prefix pattern that bypassed prefix cache warmup. I'll file CR; leaving a temp config to auto-warm new prefixes.

Jamie (sre): runbook quick pointers specific to on-call handoff:
- Primary must confirm active pages acknowledged within 2m.
- If cluster-level p99 > SLO for > 5m, escalate to on-call pager and follow major-incident checklist.
- Keep support updated every 10m while customers impacted.
- If you scale pool, watch cost dashboard and revert when stable.

Priya (platform): operational quick links for console actions:
- Console routing UI: https://console.redwood/regions/eu-west/routing
- Capacity dashboard: https://console.redwood/capacity/inference-eu
- Live traces: https://internal.redwood/traces/incident-2234

Alex (infra): leaving the following short reminders in the handoff message to next primary:
- If you run ``rwdctl capacity scale`` use ``--grace 30s`` to avoid flapping.
- For prefix throttles, prefer soft throttle first (50/s) before hard-block.
- If you see repeated KV cache evictions, consider bumping Redis maxmemory-policy from volatile-lru -> allkeys-lru for 10m window.

Mia (support): I've updated the tickets and set expected followup in 24h. acme-co asked for timeline for full postmortem.

Jamie (sre): think we can close pager as resolved; keep monitoring for 1h. I'll reduce alert sensitivity temporarily to avoid noise.

IncidentBot: Pager resolved — INCIDENT-2234 closed after 9m. Summary: routing fallback + autoscale handled most traffic.

Alex (infra): tagging this for the morning CR: will include prefix warmup, job scheduling guardrails, and a short doc on graceful model routing. leaving shift to Marcus (primary takeover) at 20:00 UTC. Marcus will be primary; I'm secondary until 20:10.

Marcus: acknowledged. I'll take over monitoring and follow up on CR drafts tomorrow. thanks for notes. :thumbsup:

Priya (platform): final checklist for handoff message to include in thread—copy this into the next primary's message so we keep consistency: "summary, customer-impact (tickets), commands used, runbook links, CR TODOs, who is primary/secondary and for how long, monitoring window."

Alex (infra): copied. handing off.
